sources.relevance: Stable Python 3.15.0 released October 9, 2026 with official regular Windows x64 artifacts. Metadata establishes artifact availability; actual application execution is recorded separately. Later stable 3.15 maintenance versions remain accepted numerically.

The final v3.15.0 source carries gh-151544's Windows Modules/Setup.local landmark fallback removal from beta 3. CVE-2026-12003 therefore does not require a later 3.15 maintenance floor; older supported branch floors remain unchanged.

The final v3.15.0 source carries gh-158010's Windows OpenSSL update to 3.5.9 from release candidate 3, addressing CVE-2026-35189 in explicit HTTPS package setup. This supports the 3.15.0 security floor without weakening existing branch floors.

Official regular Windows x64 3.15.0 SPDX metadata independently identifies bundled OpenSSL 3.5.9. This is artifact metadata evidence, not native WinBookSplit acceptance or a security guarantee for every interpreter distribution.

CVE-2026-35189 (Low): relative CRL distribution points in a peer certificate can cause disproportionate allocation during normal TLS handshake before trust rejection; no CRL-check flag is required. Explicit online pip setup uses TLS. Fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.9 (or 3.0.23); numeric floors cover the PSF Windows bundles.

gh-158010 updates Windows OpenSSL to 3.5.9. Actual tested regular x64 3.14.8 reports OpenSSL 3.5.9. Floor 3.14.8 addresses the known bundled-TLS issue; later stable maintenance versions remain accepted.

gh-158010 updates Windows OpenSSL from the 3.0 series to 3.5.9. Actual tested regular x64 3.13.16 reports OpenSSL 3.5.9. Floor 3.13.16 addresses the known bundled-TLS issue; later stable maintenance versions remain accepted.

Windows legacy all-user installs can discover attacker-controlled in-tree libraries outside the install directory. A uniform floor covers all discovery locations; protected per-user installs may be unaffected.
3.14.7 removes the Modules/Setup.local landmark fallback (gh-151544). 3.14.8 is recommended separately and later stable patches remain acceptable.
3.13.15 removes the Modules/Setup.local landmark fallback (gh-151544). 3.13.16 is recommended separately and later stable patches remain acceptable.
3.11.16 includes gh-151544 and is source-only; 3.11.9 was the last full binary release.
3.12.14 includes gh-151544 and is source-only; 3.12.10 was the last full binary release.
PSF Windows distribution URLs and hashes; all three linked catalog pages were inspected on the review date.
3.11-3.13 are security-only branches; 3.14 is in maintenance. Lifecycle status alone is not a security guarantee.
Python 3.14 supports Windows 10 and newer. Installed-runtime listing is read-only; automatic runtime installation must not be used for processing discovery.

The October 9 multiple-filter memory-consumption advisory was patched in 6.20.0; 6.21.3 retains that fix. Preserve the separate exact package lock and existing guards.

Large-array/dictionary parsing memory consumption affects versions below 6.21.0. Upstream identifies 6.21.0 as fixed; selected 6.21.3 retains the parser-limit fields. Small reduced-limit checks are separate dependency evidence, not full application or memory-sandbox acceptance.

Many-small-operation content-stream parsing memory consumption affects versions below 6.21.0. Selected 6.21.3 retains the upstream parsing-work budget. Explicit developer operations parsing does not establish application reachability or universal protection.

Its patched-version field is inconsistent with its affected range and prose; that discrepancy remains recorded in historical T08 gate-review evidence. The JPEG image-loading advisory affects versions below 6.21.1 and names 6.21.1 as fixed. Selected 6.21.3 retains that fix; production does not call image-extraction APIs, which is not a general hostile-document exemption.

Reader initialization reaches this parser before application structural preflight; preserve exact dependency, process and origin guards. This does not establish an OS memory sandbox.
